newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Senate to vote Brady bill, export tax.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Senate to vote Brady bill, export tax.

text.p: The Brazilian Senate will vote Thursday morning on a bill exempting exports from taxes and a resolution allowing the Central Bank to buy back Brady bonds and swap them for other sovereigns, officials said.
Senate officials said the upper house had scheduled a special session starting at 1030 local time/1330 GMT.

On Wednesday, government leaders struck a deal to allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to veto certain clauses from the bill exempting commodities and semi-manufactured goods from the so-called ICMS export tax.
The clauses all restrict the states from using fiscal incentives, in particular ICMS tax exemptions, to lure investors and had led to complaints from smaller states.
The Brady bond bill, which only needs Senate plenary approval to become law, would allow the Central Bank to restructure all its outstanding Bradies. It sets strict Senate oversight conditions.
Private Invest News agency reported that the Senate would vote in the afternoon a regulatory bill setting up a financial transactions tax to fund the health service, known as the CPMF cheque tax.
But Senate officials could not confirm that the CPMF had been placed on the agenda. The cheque tax bill was approved by the lower house Wednesday.
